## Automation and wiring (§20.E)
- **New script?** No. This adds one subcommand (`resolve`) to `scripts/operator_step_issue.py` and changes `scripts/activation_verify.sh` and the prompt.
- **Scheduler entry point:** `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, job `poll`. A new step, "Resolve released operator steps", goes right after "Resume dependency waits" and before "Find active tracking issues". It runs on every poller tick, with or without an active project.
- **New long-running supervisor?** No. The poller cron is the supervisor.
- **DB work:** none.
- **Entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** none, because no new script is added.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. Prompt change (both prompt files)
Make the same edit in `prompts/mode-activation-verify.txt` and `prompts/_templates/mode-activation-verify.txt`. Only the prelude differs between them.
- Line 26 / 19, the "Consumer propagation" bullet: keep it. Add that the work then stays off until the next `@stable` release, and that this is reported as described below.
- Line 32 / 25: replace "Never list promoting `main`, tagging `stable`, or the consumer sync (`AI Update Workflows` / daily wrapper sync) as a gap of either kind; the pipeline performs them." with this rule:
  - Never list promoting `main`, tagging `stable`, or the consumer sync (`AI Update Workflows` / daily wrapper sync) as an `operator` gap. The pipeline does them (`promote-main-to-stable.yml`, `update_workflows.yml`).
  - When merged work only takes effect once the next `@stable` release ships it, report that as one `code` gap with `dormant_until` set to `@stable contains <merge commit>`. The script leaves that gap to the release and opens no issue for it.
  - Secrets, repository settings and external accounts stay `operator`.
- The JSON output contract does not change. The `dormant_until` schema line may add "or `@stable contains <sha>` for a release-pending code gap".

### 2. `scripts/activation_verify.sh`
- **Compute the source SHA earlier.** Move the existing `activation_source_sha` computation up so it runs before `activation_normalise_verdict`: `MERGE_SHA` in PR mode, `git -C TARGET_DIR rev-parse HEAD` in project mode. Keep the variable names. The operator-step block reuses the value; `activation_source_args` is built as today.
- **`activation_normalise_verdict`:** add an optional third argument, the source SHA (used only when it is 40 lower-case hex). Inside the Python:
  - Add `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE = re.compile(r"^@?stable\s+contains\b", re.I)`.
  - After cleaning, a gap whose `dormant_until` matches gets `release_pending: true`.
  - A matching `operator` gap is rewritten to `kind: "code"` and gets `rerouted: true`. This is the deterministic guard against the model ignoring the prompt.
  - A release-pending gap's `dormant_until` is rewritten to `@stable contains <source sha>` when the SHA is valid; otherwise the cleaned text is kept.
  - A release-pending gap's `open_pr` is set to null.
  - Every other gap gets `release_pending: false` and `rerouted: false`.
  - Rejecting invalid verdicts works exactly as today.
- **Counts:**
  - `code_gaps` still counts all code gaps, including release-pending ones.
  - `operator_gaps` counts operator gaps after rerouting.
  - `activation_issue_gaps` becomes `kind=="code" and open_pr==null and (release_pending|not)`.
  - New count `activation_release_gaps` = `[.gaps[]|select(.release_pending)]|length`. When it is above 0, log `ACTIVATION_VERIFY mode= item= op=release_pending_gaps count=<n> rerouted=<m> outcome=left_to_release`.
- **Fix-issue body jq:** the select also excludes `release_pending`. When every code gap is release-pending or in flight, no search runs and no fix issue is created.
- **Operator steps jq:** unchanged (`select(.kind=="operator")`). Rerouted gaps are therefore never written to the operator-step issue.
- **Verdict comment gap line:** add the suffix ` (ships with the next `@stable` release; the promote cycle does this)` for release-pending gaps. The existing `open_pr` suffix stays for other gaps. The marker line does not change.
- **Telegram:** the level rule does not change. Rerouting lowers `operator_gaps`, so a release-only DORMANT verdict becomes `DEBUG`.
- **Header comment:** add a paragraph describing the release-pending handling and the new op log.

### 3. `scripts/operator_step_issue.py` — new `resolve` subcommand
- **Constants:**
  - `RESOLVED_RE = ^<!-- ai:operator-step:resolved release=stable status=(ahead|identical) -->$`
  - `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE`: the same pattern as in activation_verify. A comment in each file points at the other, and a test checks they are equal.
  - `RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE`, case-insensitive: `^(?:promote|tag|release|publish|cut|sync|propagate|roll out)\b[^\n]{0,200}?(?:@stable|\bstable\b|ai update workflows|update[ _-]workflows|wrapper sync|consumer sync)`
  - `RELEASE_ENTRY_KEY_RE = ^(?:pr|project)-[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$`
  - `AUTO_CLOSED_MARKER = "<!-- ai:operator-step:auto-closed -->"`
  - `MAX_RESOLVE_COMPARES = 10`
  - `RELEASE_REF = "stable"`
- **`operator_step_auto_resolve_enabled()`:** reads `OPERATOR_STEP_AUTO_RESOLVE_ENABLED`, default `"true"`. Only a trimmed, case-insensitive `false` disables it, the same idiom as `needs_human_enabled`.
- **`_unticked_steps(body) -> list[tuple[title, dormant]]`:** parses `- [ ] **Title**` lines. A step's dormant text is the backticked value of its following indented `Stays off until then:` line, read up to the next `- [` line.
- **`_is_release_entry(body)`:** true only when there is at least one unticked step and every unticked step either has a dormant text matching `RELEASE_CONDITION_RE` or a title matching `RELEASE_STEP_TITLE_RE`. An entry that mixes a release step with a real human step is never ticked.
- **`_release_status(repo, sha, cache)`:** calls `_gh(["api", f"repos/{repo}/compare/{sha}...{RELEASE_REF}", "--jq", ".status"])` and caches the result per SHA for the run. It returns `ahead`, `identical`, `behind`, `diverged` or `unknown`. An `ApiError` (including a 404 when `stable` does not exist, for example in a consumer repository) is re-raised to the caller. This mirrors `release_contains` in `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py`, where only `ahead`/`identical` count as contained.
- **`_render_resolved(body, status, source_sha)`:** like `_render_ticked`. Every `- [ ]` becomes `- [x]`, then it appends the `RESOLVED_RE` marker line and `Done: the `stable` tag includes the merge `<sha7>` (compare status `<status>`); ticked by the poller.`
- **`resolve(repo, trusted_login=None, max_compares=MAX_RESOLVE_COMPARES) -> dict`:**
  1. Validate the repo with `REPO_RE`. When the kill switch is off, log `OPERATOR_STEP_RESOLVE op=resolve outcome=skip reason=disabled` and return without any API call.
  2. One tracker listing, the same call as `tick` (`issues?labels=ai:operator-step&state=open&per_page=30`), filtered with `find_issues`, which keeps the needs-human digest out. With no tracker, return `issue: null` after that single call. Read the identity only after a tracker is found.
  3. Validate the tracker number the same way `tick` does. Load comments with `load_entry_comments` and pick the newest trusted comment per key with `_authoritative_entry_comments`.
  4. Go through the keys in ascending order of the authoritative comment's id (oldest first). Each key gets one outcome:
     - `already_done`: a `DONE_RE` or `RESOLVED_RE` line is present, or there is no `- [ ]` line.
     - `not_release`: the key does not match `RELEASE_ENTRY_KEY_RE`, or `_is_release_entry` is false.
     - `no_source_sha`: line 2 does not match `SOURCE_SHA_RE`.
     - `deferred`: the compare cap is reached, or compares were halted after an earlier compare error.
     - `ticked`: the status is `ahead` or `identical`. One comment POST is made.
     - `not_contained`: the status is `behind`, `diverged` or `unknown`.
     - `compare_failed`: `ApiError`. All further compares this tick are halted (fail closed, at most one wasted call
